summary.en: Use **be going to + base verb** to talk about plans you have already decided and about things you can see are about to happen: _I'm going to study law. Look at those clouds, it's going to rain._ Always use **am / is / are**: _She is going to call you._ Choosing between going to and will comes later, in Future forms.
summary.es: Be going to + verbo base sirve para planes ya decididos y para predicciones basadas en lo que ves. Necesita siempre am/is/are. La comparación con will está en la lección Future forms.

form: **Subject + am / is / are + going to + base verb**: _We are going to move house._
Negatives: **am not / isn't / aren't going to**: _I'm not going to wait._
Questions: **Am / Is / Are** + subject + **going to** + base verb: _Are you going to come? What is she going to do?_
With a place, going to is a normal verb of movement: _I'm going to the market._ You can also say _I'm going to go to the market._
Time words: **tomorrow, tonight, next week, this summer, in June**.

uses.text: **Plans and intentions** → _We're going to rent a car on holiday._
**Predictions with evidence** → _Be careful! You're going to fall._

note.en: You can see or feel the reason now.
note.es: Hay una señal clara ahora: nubes, un cielo oscuro, un vaso en el borde de la mesa.

uses.text: **Questions about plans** → _What are you going to do this weekend?_
**Refusing or deciding not to** → _I'm not going to answer that._

mistakes.wrong: I going to buy a flat.
mistakes.right: I'm going to buy a flat.

why.en: Going to always needs am, is or are.
why.es: Hace falta am/is/are antes de going to.

mistakes.wrong: She is going to buys a car.
mistakes.right: She is going to buy a car.

why.en: After to use the base verb, with no -s.
why.es: Detrás de to, verbo base: sin -s.

why.en: Going to is followed by the base verb, not by -ing.
why.es: Después de going to, verbo base, no -ing.

mistakes.wrong: Do you going to see him?
mistakes.right: Are you going to see him?

why.en: Questions with going to start with am, is or are.
why.es: La pregunta empieza con am/is/are, no con do.

mistakes.wrong: I am go to call her.
mistakes.right: I am going to call her.

examples.en: I'm going to start a new course in September.
examples.es: Voy a empezar un curso nuevo en septiembre.

examples.en: We're going to visit my cousins at the weekend.
examples.es: Vamos a visitar a mis primos el fin de semana.

examples.en: Are you going to watch the match tonight?
What are you going to wear to the wedding?
examples.es: ¿Qué te vas a poner para la boda?

examples.en: He isn't going to take the job because the pay is low.
Look at the sky! It's going to rain.
My brother and his wife are going to live in Bristol.
I'm not going to eat anything before the exam.
Is she going to meet us at the station?
They're going to paint the whole flat next month.

practice.prompt: I'm going ___ my driving test next week.

explanation.en: Going to is always followed by to + base verb.

practice.prompt: ___ you going to tell your boss about the problem?

explanation.en: Questions with going to start with are, is or am.

practice.prompt: My friends ___ going to book a table for Saturday.

explanation.en: My friends is plural, so use are.

practice.prompt: She ___ going to study medicine. She wants to be a vet.

explanation.en: The negative of going to uses isn't, not doesn't.
